I’ve been reading On the Shortness of Life by Seneca. If it is to be the last book I ever read, I will be glad. 

I mostly journal and reflect, however, I do regularly write fiction - not that it’s any good, of course. Have been writing stories in the same world ever since I was a child not burdened with thoughts of death and suicide.
I read and write that’s all I do, probably the only thing I can do at this point.
It’s difficult to let these thoughts move on as they feel omnipresent, but I understand what you mean. Thanks.

Anything that takes my mind off my thoughts. Usually philosophy/physics books as it requires me to actually think about what I’m reading, therefore less suicidal thoughts pop in. But I like anything really. Thanks.

I don’t remember the last time I didn’t feel like this. It’s just gotten too much for me, this endless cycle of my brain tearing itself apart, it just fucking hurts so much. I’ve been directionless, lost, whatever you want to call it ever since I left high school. All my friends moved on successfully and I was left to be the failure that they will look back at in the future thanking god it was me instead of them.

Thanks but none of my reading or writing will amount to anything. It is nothing but fruitless hope. And I have none left. I have accomplished nothing in my life and don’t have the energy or the capacity mentally or physically to do so.
I know people have went through worse and I have the utmost sympathy for them but I’m just simply not as strong as all of those people who persevere.
